item.title: Re: Ask The Person Above You A Question (PART IX)
item.content:encoded:
Oh man, I actually have a fun answer for this, though technically I wasn't the one operating the microwave. In college, I had a summer internship at a lab that was doing some materials science research. At some point, a couple of grad students decided they needed to very thoroughly clean some silicon wafers. One standard way to do this is with oxygen plasma, which will tear through almost anything on the surface and leave the silicon untouched. The only problem was that the lab didn't have a plasma generator.

What the lab did have, however, was a microwave. And with a bit of aluminum foil, a flask, and some water, you can use a microwave as a homemade plasma generator.

So I'm standing there, minding my own business, when they turn on the microwave and the lab lights up with this eerie blue glow as a plasma forms inside the flask. Then a couple of seconds later, there's a loud bang, the light turns orange and flickery, and there's a lot of cursing while people scramble for the fire blanket.

First thing I thought of was pepperoni pizza, and I can imagine few things that would be more disgusting than greasy cheese and slimy pepperoni floating around in milk. This cereal wouldn't even get a name, in a cereal company it wouldn't get far enough in the process to see the marketing department and be named.

Or if what you were asking is "What pizza toppings would be good in a cereal, and what would you name said cereal" then my answer would just be… cereal. Pizza has had so much stuff put onto it, I guarantee that someone at some point has straight up put cereal on pizza as a topping. Then the name of the new cereal would just be the same as the topping cereal.

item.title: Re: @forbiddenquest
item.content:encoded:
+ show block
– hide block

I'll be sent back to a largely undeveloped little island in South-east Asia. I don't have much to fear apart from the wilderness.

Firstly, I'll buy a few books from the library, as much as I can carry. Then, I'll spend the next 24 hours learning up some things online, like how to make pencils and paper and how to make fire using wood, safe ways to extract clean water, etc.

Once I'm there, I'll probably create some tools, cut down the forest around me, do a little subsistence farming/hunting-gathering and just live in a little crude mud-concrete hut for the rest of my life. I have the books to keep me company and I can write too (I'll find out a way to preserve it so that it can serve as an import archaeological find). The beasts in the forest won't see me as much of a threat and I won't bother them as well. I can study some plants, record my findings too.

Very peaceful, even if a little boring. Maybe I'll even travel to the neighbouring country by foot and find a few people to settle down and spend the rest of my life with.
